title: introduce upgrade safety protections: preflight backups, schema checks, and downgrade guard
author: Aisha Patel
ci_status: pass (initial e2e failed due to timing issue; rerun passed)
release_notes:
- Added upgrade preflight that takes and verifies backups of etcd and Terraform state.
- Added migration dry-run and post-migration verification steps.
- Implemented downgrade guard: blocks automatic downgrade if DB schema version mismatch detected.
- Helm hooks for pre-upgrade backup and post-upgrade smoke tests.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have run into subtle upgrade failures (schema drift, partial state changes) that cause manual recovery work and rollbacks. This PR adds a set of automated protections to make upgrades predictable and reversible for on-prem/VPC customers.

Summary: single PR that implements: 1) a preflight backup flow (etcd snapshot + Terraform state export + optional DB logical dump) wired into the installer CLI and Helm hooks; 2) schema migration plan and a migration dry-run mode that will validate migrations against a snapshot without committing; 3) a downgrade guard that prevents applying a lower-version release when an incompatible schema change has been observed; 4) lightweight post-upgrade verification (smoke tests) and automatic rollback trigger on critical failures; 5) documentation and operator commands for manual restore.

Checklist (what this PR includes):
- [x] installer/upgrade.go: orchestrator for preflight backup, migration dry-run, and applying migrations.
- [x] installer/rollback.go: safe rollback flow that validates backups and restores TF state + etcd.
- [x] helm/redwood/templates/preupgrade-backup-hook.yaml: Helm pre-upgrade hook that calls the installer preflight in-cluster (runs as Job).
- [x] helm/redwood/templates/postupgrade-smoke-hook.yaml: post-upgrade smoke Job; failure triggers an annotated rollback reason.
- [x] terraform/modules/installer/backup.tf: idempotent S3/KMS-backed snapshot export for Terraform state and artifacts.
- [x] db/migrations/checker.go: schema compatibility checker and version pinning metadata.
- [x] docs/upgrade-guide.md: operator-facing step-by-step with examples and runbook.
- [x] tests/e2e/upgrade-smoke.test.go: deterministic smoke tests used by Helm Job and CI.

How it works (high-level):
- The installer now runs a preflight that creates an etcd snapshot, exports the Terraform state (with a timestamped prefix), and (if requested) runs pg_dump/pg_dumpall onto an encrypted artifact store. All snapshots are validated via checksums and logged to the installer's local audit file.
- Before executing migrations we run migrations in "dry-run" mode against a restored ephemeral DB in a sidecar (if available) or via report produced by the migration library. The dry-run emits a migration plan and a compatibility score; a configured threshold can block the upgrade.
- Post-upgrade, a set of configured smoke tests (service health endpoints, basic inference path, KV cache warms) run as a Helm Job. If a smoke test fails, the installer attempts an automated rollback if the backup artifacts are available and the rollback conditions are satisfied.
- Downgrade guard: each release embeds a schema_version file in the chart. The installer compares current cluster schema_version with target. If target < current and migrations are not reversible (marker in migration metadata), the installer blocks downgrade unless --force-downgrade is passed and operator acknowledges risk. A strong warning is printed and an additional pre-downgrade backup is required when forcing.

Testing notes:
- CI: unit tests + integration harness run. The first CI run hit a timing issue in the smoke Job (flaky readiness probe); adjusted probe timeout and re-ran. Final CI status: all checks passed.
- Local manual validation: performed upgrade from 1.18.0 -> 1.19.0 on a private cluster replica; took snapshot, applied migrations in dry-run, executed migration, post-upgrade smoke tests passed. Then simulated failure and executed rollback command to validate restore flow.

Operator commands (examples):
- Preflight: ./installer upgrade --target-version 1.19.0 --preflight-only --backup-location s3://redwood-backups/cluster-xyz
- Full upgrade: ./installer upgrade --target-version 1.19.0 --backup-location s3://...
- Force downgrade (unsafe): ./installer downgrade --target-version 1.17.2 --force-downgrade --backup-location s3://...
- Manual restore: ./installer restore --backup-id 20260212-1542 --confirm

Backward compatibility and downgrade safety:
- No automatic downgrades are performed. Downgrade guard prevents common data-loss scenarios. Existing clusters that follow the normal upgrade path are unaffected. The new flags are additive and default to safe behavior (backups enabled by default).

Related: Linear ENG-2482 (upgrade reliability) and SUP-9421 support ticket triggered the initial incident that motivated this work.

Notes for reviewers: focus on the compatibility checker (db/migrations/checker.go) and the semantics around --force-downgrade. The backup artifact lifecycle and retention are intentionally out of scope for this PR (will follow-up with retention policy and automation in ENG-2610).
